name: Lion's mane jellyfish
note: Cyanea capillata: a bell as wide as a cartwheel and a mane of threads that trails for thirty metres.

name: Portuguese man o' war
note: Physalia physalis: not one animal but a colony. A float sails the surface; the threads below sting.

name: Leafy seadragon
note: Phycodurus eques: a pipefish dressed as drifting weed. The leaves are skin, not fins.

name: Ocean sunfish
note: Mola mola: the heaviest bony fish, a head with a fin above and below and no tail at all.

name: Barreleye
note: Macropinna microstoma: its head is a clear dome, and the eyes inside it turn to look straight up through it.

name: Vampire squid
note: Vampyroteuthis infernalis: neither squid nor octopus. It wraps itself in its own cloak and lights its arm tips.

name: Hatchetfish
note: Argyropelecus: thin as a blade and silver, with lights along its keel to erase its own shadow.

name: Giant siphonophore
note: Praya dubia: one of the longest animals alive, a colony of thousands strung on one stem and fishing with all of them.

name: Black seadevil
note: Melanocetus johnsonii: a globe of a fish, all mouth, fishing in the dark with a light that grows on its own head.

name: Gulper eel
note: Eurypharynx pelecanoides: a mouth that unhinges like a net, a body like a whip, and a red light at the end of it.

name: Colossal squid
note: Mesonychoteuthis hamiltoni: the heaviest invertebrate, with the largest eye of any animal, and hooks that turn in its arms.

name: Fangtooth
note: Anoplogaster cornuta: for its size, the longest teeth of any fish in the sea. Its lower fangs fold up into sockets beside its brain.

name: Dumbo octopus
note: Grimpoteuthis: the deepest-living octopus, which swims by flapping two fins like ears and drifts in its own skirt.

name: Tripod fish
note: Bathypterois grallator: it stands on the ooze on three long fin rays, faces into the current, and waits.

name: Sea pig
note: Scotoplanes: a sea cucumber that walks the abyssal plain in herds, on fat legs that are really tube feet.

name: Xenophyophore
note: Syringammina fragilissima: a single cell the size of a fist, which builds itself a house out of the sea floor.

name: Mariana snailfish
note: Pseudoliparis swirei: the deepest fish ever caught, soft as jelly, at home under eight hundred atmospheres.

name: Supergiant amphipod
note: Alicella gigantea: a beach hopper the length of a hand, scavenging at the bottom of the trenches.

name: Swimming sea cucumber
note: Enypniastes eximia: the "headless chicken monster", a sea cucumber that swims with a veil and keeps its gut behind glass.

name: A Deep One
note: An amphibious thing of the trench floor, gilled and webbed. Fishermen tell older stories about it than scientists do.

name: Father Dagon
note: It came up out of the deep and threw its arms about the stone. The stone is carved in the Drowned Script: the Sleeper sees; the tide returns.

name: Mother Hydra
note: A polyp the height of a tower, crowned with seven arms. Like the small hydras of ponds it does not grow old, and it buds daughters.

name: A shoggoth
note: A mass of bubbling, self-lit flesh that takes whatever shape it needs, pouring out of a gate in the city.

name: The Dreamer
note: Only the eye. The rest of it is the Drowned City, and the city is asleep.
